per_pair.why: Superior character art with exceptional shading and silhouette creates stronger visual appeal and first impression than a busy dungeon scene.
Cleaner, more focused menu presentation with better visual hierarchy than title-centric layout.
Shows actual responsive menu navigation with state transitions, while B shows identical repeated frames with no motion feedback.
Polished, readable upgrade selection interface with clear visual hierarchy beats repeating the title screen.

loser_biggest_gap: Menu navigation motion feedback is completely absent—the motion strip shows identical repeated frames instead of snappy transitions between menu states; add clear, responsive state changes.
loser_other_gaps: Title screen composition is too busy and unfocused; needs stronger visual hierarchy with larger, clearer character.
Dedicated settings/menu interfaces required; relying on title screen across all states feels unfinished.
Overall UI clarity and polish lag behind; interface elements should be more prominent and readable.
reasoning: A wins decisively across all four pairs with superior character art, cleaner UI design, and actual responsive menu feedback. The character-driven presentation creates immediate visual appeal and personality. B's atmospheric voxel world is thematic but lacks focus and polish. The complete absence of menu navigation motion in B's motion strip—showing only identical repeated frames—is the most glaring deficiency, undermining perceived responsiveness and feel.
